source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use an evidence-based initial full-dose regimen, then individualize subsequent dosing according to laboratory monitoring of anticoagulant effect.","B":"Keep one fixed infusion rate for adults with pulmonary embolism because coagulation studies are used only to detect bleeding, not to guide dose adjustment.","C":"Determine the final infusion rate from body weight alone and stop laboratory-guided titration once the initial calculation is completed.","D":"Adjust the infusion only according to improvement in chest pain or dyspnea because symptom response replaces anticoagulation testing during therapy."}}
source_row.rationale: Current heparin labeling states that full-dose therapy must be adjusted individually according to laboratory monitoring of anticoagulant effect. An initial dosing regimen can be protocol based, but ongoing therapeutic dosing is not determined by symptoms or body weight alone. Option A states the label-supported principle without overstating weight as the sole dosing basis.
